name: PRO ARTE Foundation
known: The site does not name the founders.

Board: Sergey Basov (vice president of the Petersburg Library Society), Elena Kolovskaya (foundation director), Irina Prokhorova (editor-in-chief of the publisher Novoe Literaturnoe Obozrenie), Leonid Romankov (state councillor of St Petersburg, first class) and Kirill Krutikov (chairman of the boar

name: Pushkinskaya-10 Art Centre
known: T-J (t-j.ru) describes Yuly Rybakov and Sergei Kovalsky as founders and Evgeny Orlov as the director.

name: State Hermitage Museum
known: Mikhail Piotrovsky has been director since July 1992.

Board of trustees: Potanin has chaired it since April 2003; members listed include Anton Siluanov, German Gref, Alexei Kudrin, Leonid Fridlyand, Mikhail Shvydkoi and Piotrovsky, with JTI Russia (LLC) as corporate member (Hermitage Friends Club, Wikipedia).
Canada sanctioned director Piotrovsky in 2023 and the EU listed him on 23 April 2026.

name: State Russian Museum
known: Founded by decision of Alexander III.
Directors: Vladimir Gusev from 1988 to 2023, then Alla Manilova since 25 April 2023 (Wikipedia).
Vladimir Gusev (director since 1988) became president in Feb 2023.
Deputy Culture Minister Alla Manilova became director on 25 Apr 2023. 3.61m visits in 2024.

name: Zarya Centre for Contemporary Art
known: Opened in 2013 on the initiative of the entrepreneur and patron Alexander Mechetin, founder and co-owner of Novabev Group, formerly Beluga Group (stated by the centre;
Alisa Bagdonaite was chief curator from 2014 to 2022 (stated by the centre).
The centre says it was launched on the initiative of Mechetin, founder and co-owner of Novabev Group, formerly Beluga Group;
ASEF Culture360 calls him founder of Russia's largest alcoholic beverage company.
AiF-Primorye (14 November 2020) calls Mechetin the founder of the centre, a patron and co-owner of Beluga Group.

name: Kramskoi Voronezh Regional Art Museum
known: Kommersant (Daria Verbitskaya, 22 September 2025) identifies Yulia Zaichenko as museum director and reports her presenting September plans at a press conference on 19 September 2025.
Founder: the Ministry of Culture of the Voronezh Region (stated by the museum on its About page).

name: Vyksa Festival (Art-Ovrag)
known: Irina Sedykh created it and chairs the board of trustees of the OMK-Uchastie charity foundation, which runs it (festival website).

name: Ural Industrial Biennial of Contemporary Art
known: Founder-commissioner Alisa Prudnikova left to run GES-2 (V-A-C).

name: Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts
known: The founder is the Department of Culture of the Yekaterinburg city administration and the director is Nikita Nikolayevich Korytin (museum website).
Founder: The museum publishes financial statements for 2014 to 2024, annual reports for 2014 to 2023 and the supervisory board's membership changes from 2017 to 2026 (museum website).

name: Yeltsin Center
known: Board of trustees: chair Anton Vaino; members include Alexander Voloshin, Naina Yeltsina, Artyom Zhoga and Denis Pasler (Yeltsin Center).
A deputy director was fined 45,000 rubles in August 2025.

name: Inema Arts Center
known: Wikipedia lists six painters, all brothers or siblings, as founders: Nkurunziza, Nkuranga, Kenneth Nkusi, Denis Mpabuka, Timothy Akimanzi and Joseph Ntwali.
On site: work by 10 local artists including co-founder Nkurunziza, and rare Congolese masks, some dating back to the 13th century (National Geographic Traveller).
The centre was founded by Nkurunziza and Nkuranga, who are painters themselves (Inema website).
Inema's site names its two founders but no funders, reports, accounts or board; a Support Inema page exists but was not readable.

name: Rwanda Art Museum
known: Director General: Robert Masozera, appointed 11 November 2020 (Rwanda Cultural Heritage Academy).

name: AlUla Arts & Cultural Oasis
known: Run by the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU), founded in July 2017 and chaired since then by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (RCU website).

name: Arts AlUla and Desert X AlUla
known: Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman chairs its board (Saudipedia).

Desert X AlUla opened its first edition from 31 January to 7 March 2020, curated by Neville Wakefield with curators Raneem Farsi and Aya Alireza, as part of Mohammed bin Salman's economic, cultural and social reform plan (Hyperallergic).
The fourth, "Space Without Measure", ran from 15 January to 28 February 2026 with 11 artists, curated by Wejdan Reda and Zoé Whitley (Desert X).

name: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra)
known: Arab News, citing the Saudi Press Agency, reported about one million visitors by October 2019 and named Fatima Al-Rashed as director.
Aramco's 11-member board includes chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan and CEO Amin H.

name: Diriyah Biennale Foundation
known: Aya Al-Bakree is chief executive (e-flux, 2025).
Editions: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale December 2021 to March 2022, curated by Philip Tinari.
Created by the Ministry of Culture, which is its responsible entity, and chaired by the culture minister (Saudipedia).
